doc.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Being city slick and playing hooky
summary: He got around New York on his own and found playing hooky pointless.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Right. And you got around the city by yourself in those times? Did you take the subway and all those kinds of things?
Oh yeah, yeah. I was city slick.

Yeah I knew how to get around and had my little ways. One day I decided to play hooky from school and found it to be the most boring thing I’d ever witnessed in my life. You know? I’d hear all these kids, “Hey I’m playing hooky tomorrow.” Man this must be great. Guess I’ll play hooky. And I played hooky and I couldn’t find anything to do because all the kids was at school, so there was nobody — oh man it was terrible, terrible. So as a result I stopped playing hooky, because I had no explanation as to where I was or what I did. And the report came back to my mother. “Where were you, what did you do?” And I..
It really wasn’t worth it. It really wasn’t.
